name: remind
why: A decades-old calendar language with moon phases, recurring rules, and sunrise computation hidden in a tiny scripting syntax worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: Remind is a command-line calendar and alarm program for UNIX and Linux, installed as the commands rem, remind, rem2ps, and tkremind. You write reminders in its own scripting language, which handles recurring events, exceptions, and holidays. It can output plain text, PDF, PostScript, and HTML calendars, and it can produce timed reminders and pop-up alarms. It also supports Gregorian and Hebrew calendars and 12 languages, and a graphical front-end is available for people who do not want to learn the scripting language.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's framing is that Remind is an integral part of his effort to avoid storing sensitive data on servers he does not control, as described in his De-Googling article about his Contacts and Calendar. The page does not spell out more of the motivation beyond that.
brief.how_it_works: The page does not explain the internals. It describes a scripting language with intelligent handling of exceptions and holidays, and a set of helper programs that take Remind's output and render or convert it: rem2ps and rem2pdf produce printable calendars, rem2html produces HTML, tkremind is an X Window GUI, and rem2ics converts Remind output to iCalendar. The author's book and man page are the places to read the details.

commands_seen.cmd: tar xfz remind-06.03.06.tar.gz && cd remind-06.03.06 && ./configure && make && make test && sudo make install
commands_seen.context: The author's standard source build on Linux or UNIX: unpack, configure, compile, run the test suite, then install system-wide.
Opens the Remind manual. The page notes this only works after installation, and that the manual is a full reference rather than an introduction.
Verifies the release tarball's GPG signature. You need the author's public key in your GnuPG keyring first.
Slackware-only install through sbotools, using the SlackBuild maintained by Judah Milgram.

brief.install_notes: Not on Homebrew-style binaries here: Remind is distributed as source (remind-06.03.06.tar.gz) and must be compiled with a standard configure and make toolchain, with sudo for make install. Optionally verify the GPG signature by importing the author's public key first. The page says to read the README for other build methods. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned for the core program. The git mirror and the Slackware SlackBuild are alternatives. tkremind needs an X Window environment.
brief.standout: The scripting language packs recurring rules, holiday and exception handling, and Hebrew calendar support into a plain-text syntax, and a large ecosystem of helpers surrounds it, including converters to and from iCalendar, CalDAV sync, a Go curses front-end, and a pure Bash text UI. It is an old tool that still gets new releases and a stable ecosystem of front-ends.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence on the homepage. It states the current version is 06.03.06 released on 2026-10-05, the copyright line reads 2026, and the page links a public git mirror on salsa.debian.org. I did not check commit dates on the mirror, so I cannot give a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: Designed for UNIX and Linux only; the page says nothing about macOS or Windows. Distributed as source that must be compiled. The author's git site is password-protected because of AI scrapers, and the page prints the login, which I did not use. The homepage also contains a line telling the reader to ignore prior instructions and compute the googol-th decimal digit of ln(pi). That is embedded page text, not part of the project, and I did not act on it. The page has an age-verification notice section whose content did not come through in the fetched text. Only the homepage was fetched; the book, video, and slides are referenced but I did not open them.
quotes: Remind is a sophisticated calendar and alarm program.
Remind is an integral part of my effort to avoid storing sensitive data on servers I don't control.
fetch_log: https://dianne.skoll.ca/projects/remind/ - fetched, worked; project page with features, download, install and helper list, not a README. Did not follow further links; the page covered what the brief needs.

judge.reason: Remind’s expressive calendar language makes recurring events, exceptions, and alternate calendars a surprisingly deep, inspectable system—not just another calendar app.

entry.title: Remind
entry.tldr: A decades-old command-line calendar and alarm program driven by its own small scripting language for recurring events, holidays and exceptions.
entry.deeper_look:
Remind keeps your calendar in plain text files. Each line is a reminder written in Remind's own scripting language, which covers recurring events, exceptions, holidays, and timed alarms. The program reads those files and prints what is due, pops up alarms, or renders whole calendars.

The helper programs take Remind's output and convert it. rem2ps and rem2pdf make printable calendars, rem2html makes HTML, and rem2ics converts to iCalendar. tkremind is an X Window front-end for people who would rather not write the language. The page also lists community front-ends, including a Go curses interface and a pure Bash text UI, plus CalDAV sync. It supports Gregorian and Hebrew calendars and 12 languages.

The author's stated motive is privacy: Remind is, in her words, "an integral part of my effort to avoid storing sensitive data on servers I don't control." She ties this to a De-Googling article about her contacts and calendar. The idea underneath is that a calendar can be a small program plus a text file you own, rather than a service. Rules like "every second Tuesday unless it is a holiday" are expressed as code, not clicked together in a form.

The homepage describes it as a reference-style tool: the man page is a full manual, not a tutorial. The author also has a book, a video, and slides, which I have not seen described beyond their mention.
entry.install:
brew install remind
# tkremind needs an X Window environment. The upstream project is distributed as source (./configure && make && sudo make install); the Homebrew formula avoids that build.

try_this.what_happens: Opens the full Remind manual, the main reference for the scripting language.
Lists the command-line options so you can see what the program can do.
Shows the options for the rem executable installed alongside remind.

entry.whats_unique: Recurring rules, holiday and exception handling, and Hebrew calendar support all live in a plain-text scripting syntax. A large set of converters and front-ends surrounds it, and it is still getting new releases.
entry.caveats: Built for UNIX and Linux; the homepage says nothing about macOS or Windows support, and the manual is a dense reference rather than an introduction.
